summary: Use the ssh connection type (native OpenSSH) instead of paramiko to get connection reuse via ControlPersist, Kerberized SSH and your local SSH config; old OpenSSH on RHEL 6 or SLES 10/11 may not support ControlPersist.
questions: How do I make Ansible use my ~/.ssh/config?
How do I enable SSH connection reuse?
Does Ansible support Kerberos SSH login?
Should I use paramiko or ssh?

answer_card.title: Use OpenSSH for ControlPersist and ssh config
answer_card.answer_md:
Use the **`ssh`** connection (native OpenSSH) via `-c ssh` or in ansible.cfg:

```ini
[defaults]
transport = ssh
```

That gives ControlPersist connection reuse, Kerberos/GSSAPI and `~/.ssh/config` support. It's the default when OpenSSH supports ControlPersist. On very old OpenSSH (RHEL 6, SLES 10/11) run Ansible from a newer control host or use paramiko.
